### 1. Restate the issue in one sentence before editing
The `separability_matrix` function incorrectly reports non-separable outputs for a nested compound model (`Pix2Sky_TAN() & (Linear1D(10) & Linear1D(5))`) because `_cstack` fails to properly offset and place the coordinate matrix of the right-hand side sub-model when it is itself a `CompoundModel`, causing its internal axes to overlap with those of the left-hand side.

### 2. Inspect the smallest plausible set of source files
The bug resides in **`astropy/modeling/separable.py`**, specifically within the `_cstack` function (lines ~136–157). The logic assumes that if `right` is a `Model`, it can be directly passed to `_coord_matrix`. However, when `right` is a `CompoundModel`, `_coord_matrix` recursively calls itself on its children. Crucially, the recursive call inside `_cstack` (via `_coord_matrix`) does not account for the fact that the *entire* right-hand side compound model has already been processed by `_separable` to produce an intermediate matrix in other contexts, but here we are building up from primitives.
